h: Yisrael Helps Bring the Holiness of the Kohanim Into Being

p: it counts that everything in the world
יֵשׁ לוֹ מְצִיאוּת בְּעוֹלָם שָׁנָה נֶפֶשׁ
that is, in place, in time and in souls.
Now the holiness of the Mikdash
the holiness of Shabbos is in time,
and in souls they are the Kohanim,
who are the counterpart of the holiness
which is holier than all the lands
and is also called the Holy Land,
as against the land of the nations,
and so Yisrael as against the nations
to be sanctified as holy of holies,
like the place of the Mikdash,
Now in this parashah we find
written five times regarding the Kohanim
"They shall be holy to their God,"
"for he is holy to his God,"
are from the side of Hashem Yisbarach,
as it says, "to their God," "to his God";
which are alluded to in the pasuk,
holy on earth, the work of His might,
holy forever and for all eternity."
"Holy on earth, the work of His might"
alludes to the Friday night meal,
which is a person's own effort,
"What does Hashem your God ask of you
and this is the attribute of Gevurah.
This is the "field of holy apples,"
which are called the souls of Yisrael:
to receive the holiness of Shabbos,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זוֹהַר חֵלֶק א ה, ב)
And "Holy in the highest heavens above"
is only from the side of Hashem Yisbarach;
and of Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him, it says
and of the creation of the world it says,
And "Holy forever and for all eternity"
which corresponds to Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
which is the permanence and endurance
וּשְׂפַת אֱמֶת תִּיכּוֹן לָעַד (מִשְׁלֵי יב, יט)
and "The lip of truth shall be established forever" (Mishlei 12:19).
"They shall be holy to their God"
should make effort on their part
that the holiness should be in them
"for he is holy to his God"
that it is from his own self and root;
"to his God" — from the side of Hashem Yisbarach.
that the Beis Din shall sanctify him
and "He shall be holy to you":
that you treat him with holiness,
and in the Gemara, Moed Katan 28b).
are only from the side of the holiness of Yisrael,
"From him the peg, from him the cornerstone,"
"From him its Kohanim, from him its kings, etc."
only that the Kohanim were chosen
for from the holiness of Yisrael
the holiness of the Kohanim emanates.
וְכְדִבְרֵי רַבֵּינוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ זֵכֶר צַדִּיק לִבְרָכָה
This accords with the words of our holy Rebbe, zt"l,
Why do the Kohanim not recite
each day, "Who made me a Kohen"?
do not recite "Who made me a Yisrael,"
but only "Who did not make me a gentile" and "a slave";
nor do we recite "Who made me a man,"
but only "Who did not make me a woman"
in the Taz and Magen Avraham there).
And the reason one does not recite
and by the name Yisrael is called
one who has chosen the good;
whether he can stand firm in his choice?
"Who did not make me a gentile" and "a slave";
וְעַל כָּל פָּנִים נִיתַּן תַּחַת הַבְּחִירָה
at least he has been given free choice
because he is not a gentile or a slave;
and likewise "Who did not make me a woman,"
and it is in his choice to fulfill all the mitzvos
in which a man is commanded beyond a woman.
And likewise with a Kohen, it is not fitting to recite
for here too the choice is in his hand
to instill the holiness in his heart,
and he must also take care
And "Who did not make me a Yisrael"
and chas v'shalom to say so.
And he agreed with my words,
that it is a true answer.
for all the holiness in them
between the Tannaim in the Mishnah
between the Court of Yisrael and the Court of the Kohanim"
that is, there were no steps
between the Court of Yisrael and the Court of the Kohanim,
there was a step, and it was a cubit high."
And it is hinted that the first Tanna holds
שֶׁאֵין לְכֹהֵן שׁוּם מַעֲלָה עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל
that a Kohen has no superiority over a Yisrael,
for the holiness of the Kohanim
comes from the holiness of Yisrael,
"From him the peg, from him the cornerstone";
and Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov holds
that there was one step there.
And it is known that in all disputes,
are the words of the living God,"
for the aspect of extra superiority
הוּא גַּם כֵּן מִצַּד קְדוּשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל
also comes from the holiness of Yisrael.
written at the end of the passage
allude to the holiness of the Kohanim
that comes from the holiness of Yisrael;
and just as Yisrael sanctify Shabbos,
although it is a holiness from Hashem Yisbarach
כֵּן הֵם גַּם כֵּן מְקַדְּשִׁים לַכֹּהֲנִים
so too they sanctify the Kohanim.
we find that in the First Tablets
it says "Remember, etc., to sanctify it,"
"a place where there is no forgetting."
that this is why it says
for at the time of Mattan Torah
the words of Torah were fixed in their heart
(as they said in Shir HaShirim Rabbah
through remembering it with the mouth,
the holiness of Shabbos would at once be fixed
and no guarding would be needed;
and will not do work on it,
for the holiness of Shabbos is fixed in him.
And in the Second Tablets it is written "Keep,"
for the permanence in the heart was not
with which Yisrael sanctify the Kohanim:
the first, "And you shall sanctify him,"
is the instilling of the holiness;
וְאַחַר כָּךְ כִּי קָדוֹשׁ הוּא לָךְ
and afterward, "for he is holy to you"
that is, that it is already fixed in the heart
And at the end of the five holinesses it is written,
כִּי קָדוֹשׁ אֲנִי ה׳ מְקַדִּשְׁכֶם (שָׁם, ח)
"For I, Hashem Who sanctifies you, am holy" (Vayikra 21:8):
"For I, Hashem Who sanctifies you, am holy";
just as they said regarding the festivals,
that it is because they are holy.
a parable of a king and a noblewoman:
so "I am holy, you are holy."
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר כִּי קָדוֹשׁ אֲנִי ה׳
And this is what it says: "For I, Hashem, am holy,"
and through this I sanctify you
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה אַתֶּם יְכוֹלִים גַּם כֵּן
and through this you too can
which is from the side of Hashem Yisbarach.

inlineHeadings.text: Five Holinesses in the Priestly Calling
Yisrael Sanctifies the Kohanim From Its Own Holiness
Inherited Holiness Still Requires Human Choice
Remembering and Guarding Make Holiness Last
